rules.justification: Linear static solve. Measured per case (parameters.conditioning, probe v2): cond2(K_ff) = 1.06 / 10.73 / 3.79 / 10.54 (patch_triangle_3 / quadrangle_8 / tetrahedron_4 / hexahedron_20; 2-21 free DOFs) and normwise backward error of the oracle solve 6.1e-17 to 8.3e-17 (aarch64, variant aarch64-auto) and 3.1e-17 to 1.26e-16 (x86_64 golden, OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell; cond2 identical to 13 digits on both). A faithful port with another backward-stable factorisation (backward error <= ~10 u) differs by <= cond2 (eta_oracle + eta_port) <= 10.54 (1.26e-16 + 1.11e-15) = 1.3e-14 in the 2-norm (eta_port dominates, so the bound holds for both platforms' goldens); converting to a per-component maximum (sqrt(n) <= 4.6, smallest component maximum >= 0.37 of the largest) gives <= ~1.6e-13, i.e. a >= 60x margin to 1e-11. Patch-test solutions are the exact affine field (reproduced to 2e-16 by the oracle). Stresses are B u times the constitutive matrix (kernel rounding ~1e-14), carrying the solve error of the gradient. Explicit whole-tensor scale, not per (row, col): a component's rounding is set by the whole gradient, and components that vanish analytically are rounding noise (sigma_yz of patch_hexahedron_20 is 2e-16 of max|sigma|, measured; eps_yz(A) = 0).
rules.evidence: Cross-solver rule (oracle MUMPS vs port Eigen SparseLU), 2026-11-11: an independent review measured the port (Eigen SparseLU) against the oracle (MUMPS): displacement and internal force max relative difference 1.4e-16 to 8.5e-16 on the 4 patch cases (rule 1e-11: margin >= 1e4); everything that does not depend on the factorisation (K, f_ext, iteration count, assembly from the oracle's u) is bitwise; Eigen-pinned bitwise twins: fixtures/model/smm/patch_static_elastic_{triangle_3,quadrangle_8,tetrahedron_4,hexahedron_20}.

rules.justification: Limited-purpose diagnostic, not a convergence check. Whether the port's own solve stops correctly is checked separately by solver acceptance (akantu_validation::solver, run automatically whenever newton/* convergence quantities are checked: |r_n| < 1e-10 |r_0| first reached at the recorded iteration, iteration count / residual history / error consistent), and newton/nb_iterations is compared exactly. This rule only bounds how far the port's final residual |r_n| (N) lies from the oracle's: it flags a port that stops at the same iteration on a residual far from the oracle's (e.g. near the stopping level where the oracle's is rounding noise), which acceptance and the per-step history rule (1e-8 |r_0| ~ 5e-3 N) would both allow. Final residuals: step 1 (elastic, one iteration) 1.06e-9 N (aarch64 variant; 1.03e-9 N on the x86_64 golden, OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell), pure rounding noise of the residual evaluation; steps 2-5 (plastic, 14-21 iterations, linear contraction 0.28-0.34) 2.4e-5 to 8.3e-5 N, set by the truncation of the iteration, with rounding-sensitive trailing digits (|J_ff|_2 = 2.6e12 N/m). Magnitude: measured strict-vs-default variation of this case (same algorithm; FMA contraction and NEON vectorisation on/off) <= 5.1e-10 N with identical iteration counts (step 1: 5.1e-10 N, 48% of its value; steps 2-5: 3.1e-11 to 3.2e-10 N); sensitivity indicators: |J_ff|_2 x 1e-20 m = 2.6e-8 N, |J_ff|_2 x one spacing of the recorded displacements = 5e-9 to 1.3e-8 N. 1e-7 N is ~200x the measured variation and ~4x the largest indicator (a port with another assembly order or factorisation varies more than strict vs default), hence no evidence of rounding-level equivalence either; it is 240x below the smallest plastic final residual and 485x below the smallest stopping level (4.85e-5 N, step 1).
rules.evidence: strict-vs-default variation measured on this case with the default install (indicative: install-default not yet validated for baseline use), docs/NUMERICAL_VALIDATION.md section 7. Measured 2026-11-11: MUMPS (oracle) vs Eigen SparseLU (port) final residuals differ by <= 4.8e-10 N on aarch64 and x86_64; strict vs default oracle <= 5.1e-10 N; residual evaluation noise about 1e-9 N.

rules.justification: Newmark (trapezoidal) steps of the plastic patch model/implicit_dynamic/patch_triangle_6_plastic (oracle MUMPS, port Eigen SparseLU; Newton-Raphson, |r_k| < 1e-10 |r_0|, 14-21 iterations per step, newton/nb_iterations compared exactly). Solve error: cond2(J_ff) = 28.5. Two backward-stable factorisations (MUMPS, SparseLU), each with backward error ≲ 10u, differ per solve by ≲ cond2·(η1 + η2) ≈ 6e-14 of the increment. Damping and accumulation: the Newton contraction ρ ≤ 0.34 damps this by 1/(1 − ρ) ≤ 1.5. Five steps of an unconditionally stable scheme with a non-expansive radial return accumulate it to ≲ 5e-13 of the step maximum for u. Acceleration: the trapezoidal update a_{n+1} = 4(u_{n+1} − u_n)/Δt² − 4v_n/Δt − a_n amplifies relative differences by ≈ 4‖u‖/(Δt²‖a‖); the measured a/u ratio is ≈ 70. A priori ≲ 3.5e-11 for a, the worst quantity. Measured per step: u 4.3e-16, v 1.44e-14, a 2.9e-14, energies 7.5e-16 (identical on aarch64 and x86_64). Strict vs default oracle: ≤ 1.9e-14, and ≤ 5.2e-15 of the row maximum for residual histories. 1e-10 is 3× the a-priori bound and ≈ 3,400× the largest measured difference. It still separates algorithmic deviations (≥ 1e-3, or changed iteration counts), and it is 100× tighter than the former placeholder bound. The residual-history tails it will cover once the port exposes per-iteration norms agree to ≈ 2e-15 of the row maximum (final residuals differ by 4.8e-10 N against |r₀| ≥ 2.4e5 N). The justification depends on this case's conditioning, so future cases need their own measured cond₂ (and their own rule). Scale: per step (ragged rows for the residual histories). Energies: one scalar per step.
rules.evidence: 2026-11-11: per-step relative differences of the port's replay (crates/akantu-solid/tests/model_fixtures.rs::implicit_dynamic_plastic_patch_replay; Mac and x86_64, identical): u <= 4.3e-16, v <= 1.44e-14, a <= 2.9e-14, energies <= 7.5e-16; indicative strict-vs-default oracle measurement (2026-11-10): <= 1.9e-14 of the step maximum for u, v, a, energies and f_ext + f_int, <= 5.2e-15 of the row maximum for the residual histories. Was PROPOSED rel 1e-8 on model/implicit_dynamic/* (2026-11-09); tightened to 1e-10 and narrowed to this case.
